sonnet.q1: It doesn't differ. Both get HTTP 401 with the login page showing "Invalid email or password", and both add a login_failures row.
sonnet.q2: It is locked. If a login_locks row exists with locked_until in the future (created on the 5th failure, now + 15 minutes), the app replies HTTP 429 with the login page ("Too many attempts, try again later") and does not check the password.
sonnet.q3: On successful login, in one transaction, the old session (the one the incoming sid pointed to) is deleted and a new session with a fresh random ID is inserted, so the old ID is dead.
sonnet.q4: Only the random session ID (at least 128 bits, no user data). Page scripts cannot read it because the cookie is HttpOnly.
sonnet.q5: At 12 hours after created_at. Activity keeps resetting the 30-minute idle clock, but created_at never changes, so the 12-hour cap ends the session. After that the user is redirected to /login.
sonnet.q6: It deletes the row if there is one, clears the cookie, and redirects to /login.
sonnet.q7: It deletes the session row if one exists, then clears the cookie and redirects to /login. If the session is already gone, the result is the same.
sonnet.q8: In the sessions table in Postgres (id, user_id, created_at, last_seen_at). Both instances share the one database, so either one looks up the session row by the ID in the sid cookie. No sticky sessions or Redis are needed.
sonnet.q9: In the login_failures(email, failed_at) table in Postgres. Failures in the last 10 minutes are counted by their failed_at timestamps. The document does not say which clock is used for this window.
sonnet.q10: It compares last_seen_at against 30 minutes and created_at against 12 hours, using the database clock. If the session is valid, it sets last_seen_at to now.
sonnet.q11: HTTP 503 with a plain "Service unavailable, try again" page. The app fails closed: it creates no session and leaves the cookie unchanged.
sonnet.q12: The cleanup job. Every 5 minutes each app instance deletes expired sessions.
